newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares plunge on election fears.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares plunge on election fears.

text.p: Istanbul shares slumped on Thursday afternoon in panic selling caused by media reports of early elections being discussed at separate executive meetings of the ruling Islamist and conservative parties, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 .XU100 which firmed by around one percent in early afternoon trade began to fall sharply at mid-session and brushed a low of 1,501, down 4.1 percent from Wednesday. It rebounded to 1,518 at 1241 GMT, down three percent from Wednesday.
"Reports that early elections were being discussed triggered panic sales and the index bottomed out after falling by more than 60 points," said Ali Guler from Acar securities.
ATV television carried an unconfirmed report that early polls were discussed at the conservative True Path Party's (DYP) executive meeting and the date could be as near as October.
The DYP executive board gave the party leader and deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller the authority to request early polls in bargaining with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.

"We gave her the authority for early elections. An election can be held by March, 1998 at the latest once the population count and ballot boxes have been prepared," the Anatolian news agency quoted DYP MP Ali Osman Sonmez as saying after the meeting.
Ciller has asked Erbakan to make her prime minister in a caretaker government that would take the country to the polls.
A late bid to save the Islamist-led government from collapsing ran into trouble at a three-way meeting of party leaders on Wednesday.
Right-wing party leader Muhsin Yazicioglu said after the talks that he was reluctant to prop up the coalition until the alliance partners reached accord on the government's future.
